To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the therapeutic strategy of inducing structural repair in the injured spinal cord by transplanting adult NPCs, after successful propagation from a minimal biopsy, is feasible at preclinical level.

adult autologous neural progenitor cells, isolated from minimal brain biopsies and propagated separately for 8 weeks, can be transplanted into the spinal cord in a clinically relevant preclinical model of spinal cord injury.

the transplantation of autologous adult NPCs, after the propagation of these cells from a small aspiration biopsy, represents an effective strategy for promoting structural repair of the chronically injured CNS, which is based on a single preclinical animal study.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a cell-based therapeutic strategy that is based on the transplantation of adult autologous neural progenitor cells into a spinal cord lesion in rats.
the generation of autologous adult neural progenitor cells for cell-based therapy of chronic spinal cord injury.
the development of novel cell-based regenerative approaches in the treatment of spinal cord injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transplantation of autologous adult NPCs into a spinal cord lesion site, which were propagated for 8 weeks after a minimal subventriculuar zone biopsy, is feasible and can promote substantial tissue replacement, glial differentiation and axonal regeneration.
the autologous transplantation strategy of adult NPCs represents an effective strategy to promote structural regeneration and functional recovery after spinal cord injury.
the transplantation of adult autologous neural progenitor cells represents a feasible and attractive strategy to promote structural CNS repair in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
autologous transplantation strategies are feasible and can be used in preclinical models of CNS disease.
autologous NPCs represent a promising source for cell-based strategies in spinal cord injury.
the therapeutic strategy of transplanting adult autogenous NPCs, after the generation from a small biopsy into an acute spinal cord injury, appears feasible at the pre-clinical level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to isolate and propagate adult NPCs from a minimal brain biopsy and transplant them into the injured spinal cord in an autologus fashion, thus avoiding the need for immune suppression.

the therapeutic strategy of autologous adult NPC transplantation after a successful biopsy and propagation in a CNS disease model, e.g. spinal cord injury, can be achieved in a relevant pre-clinical animal model.

autologous transplantation strategies, such as the transplantation of adult autologous neural progenitor cells, are not only feasible, but may also be more effective than syngenic cell-based therapies in the future.
